cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO

govern.name: Governance

stories.head: Stonly Launches Business Process Agents to Automate End-to-End Customer Service
stories.plain: Stonly's new Business Process Agents let AI follow the same knowledge bases and SOPs support teams already use — no rebuilding required. This matters because it lowers the barrier to deploying agentic automation in customer service, letting brands hand off complex multi-step processes to AI without rewriting their institutional knowledge from scratch.

stories.head: Fingerprint Launches Bot Directory to Map AI Crawlers and Automated Web Traffic
stories.plain: Fingerprint released a public, searchable Bot Directory cataloguing AI crawlers and bots hitting websites. As generative AI search engines index the web more aggressively, marketers and site owners need to know which bots are real and which are scrapers — this tool directly supports both GEO strategy and traffic-quality governance.

stories.head: accessiBe Code Agent Brings Agentic Accessibility Review Into GitHub Pull Requests
stories.plain: accessiBe's Code Agent reviews accessibility compliance at the pull-request stage, before code ships. For MarTech builders, this represents a new class of agentic governance baked directly into developer workflows — catching compliance issues early rather than retrofitting fixes after launch, reducing legal and reputational risk.

stories.head: Hybrid E-Commerce Playbook: One Platform Serving Both B2B and B2C Buyers
stories.plain: Guy Gunter Home's rebuild with agency OX shows how a single intelligent commerce platform can serve two fundamentally different buying modes without fragmenting the brand. The case study is practical for teams deciding how to architect personalization and data infrastructure that handles both wholesale and retail customers from one stack.

stories.head: cPanel AI Brings Generative Website and App Creation to Global Hosting Providers
stories.plain: cPanel's generally available AI layer lets hosting providers offer AI-generated website and application creation directly within their platform. For MarTech teams, this signals that generative site-building is moving from premium SaaS tools into commodity hosting infrastructure — reshaping how small and mid-market brands launch AI-assisted digital experiences.

stories.head: AI Search Is Rewriting Brand Visibility — Earned Media Is Becoming Infrastructure
stories.plain: The piece argues that generative AI answer engines are now the gatekeepers of brand discovery, shifting the question from search ranking to AI credibility signals. For marketers, this reframes earned media — press, reviews, citations — as foundational infrastructure for GEO strategy, not just PR. Anyone buying or building visibility programs needs to understand this shift now.

stories.head: Stensul Integrates Governed Creation With Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next for AI-Driven Campaigns
stories.plain: Stensul's beta integration lets marketers and AI agents build and personalize campaigns inside Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next while enforcing brand and compliance guardrails throughout creation. This matters because it shows how governed agentic content creation is being wired directly into major CEPs — changing how enterprise teams buy and configure marketing stacks.

stories.head: Stonly Launches Business Process Agents to Automate End-to-End Customer Service Workflows
stories.plain: Stonly's new Business Process Agents run complete customer service workflows autonomously, following existing SOPs and knowledge bases rather than requiring teams to rebuild processes for AI. This is a meaningful shift in how agentic AI is deployed in service operations — reusing human-designed rules rather than replacing them — with direct implications for governance and accountability.

stories.head: Vibe Expands Connected TV Platform With Agent Access via Claude, ChatGPT, and Open APIs
stories.plain: Vibe now lets advertisers launch and manage streaming TV campaigns directly through AI agents like Claude and ChatGPT, or via their own applications. This is an early real-world example of agentic media buying — where an AI system, not a human in a UI, controls campaign decisions and spend — a model likely to spread across programmatic channels.

stories.head: Fingerprint Launches Public Bot Directory to Map AI Crawlers and Automated Web Traffic
stories.plain: Fingerprint's searchable Bot Directory catalogs AI tools, crawlers, and bots hitting websites, giving organizations a way to distinguish human from automated traffic. As AI agents increasingly act on the web on behalf of users and brands, knowing which traffic is bot-generated becomes critical for analytics accuracy, ad fraud prevention, and governance of automated systems.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Becoming Operational Infrastructure
body: Across customer service, connected TV, and developer workflows, AI agents are no longer demos — they are being embedded directly into production systems. Stonly's Business Process Agents automate complex service flows, Vibe adds agent access to its CTV platform, and accessiBe ships a Code Agent that bakes accessibility into developer pipelines.

The decision-shift here is that buying a point tool is no longer the question; the question is which platforms expose agent interfaces and which lock you out. Marketers who pick closed stacks now will find themselves manually bridging workflows their competitors automate end-to-end.

themes.head: AI Search Rewrites Brand Visibility Rules
body: AI-powered search engines are reshuffling which brands surface in answers, making earned media — press coverage, reviews, citations — function as technical infrastructure rather than a soft PR metric. Brands that historically relied on paid search dominance are discovering their presence in AI-generated responses depends on what third parties say about them, not what they bid.

This forces a strategic reallocation: content and PR investments now carry SEO-equivalent weight, and teams must treat authoritative external mentions as a pipeline asset. The window to build this corpus before AI search matures is narrow.
ev: Agile Brand · AI Search & Earned Media

themes.head: Governance Layers Enter AI-Powered Creation
body: Stensul's integration with Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next signals a maturing phase: guardrails, brand controls, and approval workflows are being baked into AI content creation rather than bolted on afterward. This is the industry acknowledging that speed without governance creates compliance and brand-consistency risk at scale.

For marketing ops leaders, the practical implication is that choosing a content creation platform now means evaluating its governance architecture, not just its generative output quality. Teams that skip this will face audit failures and brand dilution as AI-generated volume grows.
ev: Stensul · Governed Creation in SFMC Next
Agile Brand · MarTech & CX News Sept 18

themes.head: Bot & Traffic Intelligence Becomes a First-Line Defense
body: Fingerprint's Bot Directory — built explicitly for the AI era — reflects a sharp escalation in automated traffic complexity. As AI agents proliferate and interact with websites, the line between legitimate automation and adversarial bots dissolves, making bot classification a prerequisite for accurate analytics, ad measurement, and fraud prevention.

Marketers can no longer treat bot filtering as a backend IT concern. Unfiltered AI-agent traffic will corrupt conversion data, inflate media costs, and skew personalization models — meaning bot intelligence now belongs in the MarTech stack evaluation criteria alongside CDPs and attribution tools.
ev: Agile Brand · MarTech & CX News Sept 17

themes.head: Retail & Commerce Channels Collide Into Full-Funnel Media
body: DoorDash's framing of retail media as a full-funnel channel — from awareness to doorstep delivery in 30 minutes — combined with the hybrid B2B & B2C e-commerce playbook signals that the distinction between commerce and media is collapsing. Platforms that carry transactions are becoming ad networks, and ad networks are adding purchase rails.

For brand planners, this means campaign planning must now account for conversion happening inside media environments that also control logistics and inventory data. Budgets siloed in 'retail' versus 'brand' categories will misallocate as these channels merge.

month.takeaway: Every major move this month points to the same underlying shift: AI is no longer a feature inside MarTech tools but the connective tissue reorganizing which platforms, data, and channels hold strategic leverage — and teams that treat it as an add-on will cede ground to those rebuilding their stacks around it.
